title: Hand over a rejected message without handing over the card

blocks.text: The acquirer's host has started rejecting some purchases with response code 30, and its support desk wants to see what your client sent. `DeclineReport` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/DeclineReport.java` is what the client hands over for each rejection: an entry in the node's log, which your own team compares with the host's trace, and a hex dump that goes by e-mail to the support desk, which works for another company.

The node's log is shipped to a platform that many people can search. Neither the log entry nor the dump may carry card data. The support desk is hunting a format error, so the dump must still be the message as their host received it. And the client keeps the request after reporting it, because it may need it for a reversal.
Finish the two methods marked `TODO`: `logRejection` and `shareableImage`. About a dozen lines in total.

The tests give the report the node's logger, with `ProtectedLogListener` in front of a writer, and the `iso87ascii` packager. The messages carry a track 1, a track 2 and a PIN block as well as the card number.

cases.says: the log entry shows the request and the rejection field by field
the dump for the support desk is an image of the rejected request that the packager can read back
the messages go into the entry as ISOMsg objects, so the filter masks them; a wrapper that dumps them itself passes card data through
the bytes are text the filter never sees, so the card number is masked in what gets packed
the binary secrets are blanked too, not only the card number and track data
masking is done on a copy, so the client's own message keeps its real card data
card fields are masked rather than removed, so the dump keeps the host's lengths and bitmap

origin.section: 8.4 Bytes and Packager Traces Are Text Too

concepts: Hex dumps and packager traces are text no filter touches; a dump to share is made from a masked copy, which keeps the lengths and bitmap the host saw.
ProtectedLogListener masks a copy of each ISOMsg that is itself a message of the event; strings and wrappers that dump messages themselves pass through in clear.
